issues.description: The problem statement (UML and description) requires a Stock.emptyStock() method, but the template Stock.java provides clearInventory() while the solution uses emptyStock(). This method-name mismatch between the problem statement and the template can confuse students about which method to implement/use and causes a structural inconsistency between template and expected design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either rename template's clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or update the problem statement/UML to refer to clearInventory(). Ensure the template, UML, and solution all use the same method name/signature (emptyStock(): void) so students know which method to implement/ call.

issues.description: The problem description instructs that the SealSaloon.stock should be initialized to a default value in the (instance) constructor, but elsewhere the statement requires that the stock attribute be static/shared across all instances. Initializing a static field in an instance constructor is contradictory (and atypical), which creates confusion about whether stock should be an instance or static field and where it should be initialized.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement: either require stock to be a static field and specify it should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer, or require it to be an instance (non-static) final field and be initialized in the instance constructor. Update the instructions so they do not ask students to both make stock static and initialize it in the instance constructor.

issues.description: The problem statement (and the solution) refer to a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template Stock class provides a method named clearInventory() for the same functionality. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual operation (clearing the stock) can confuse students mapping the requirement to the template code and the expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (or add a delegating emptyStock() method that calls clearInventory()) so the template, problem statement, and solution use the same identifier for clearing the stock.
